name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 26
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 26

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset multisystemic involvement including neurological and muscular symptoms
Deficient activity of multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with oxidative phosphorylation defects
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia or brainstem abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus biochemical evidence and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data.

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Deficient activity of multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes in muscle biopsy
imaging: MRI brain showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated complex I deficiency rather than combined defects
Different genetic mutations affecting complex I subunits
Characteristic symmetrical necrotizing lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
Often caused by mutations in mitochondrial or nuclear genes distinct from COXPD26

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deterioration in infancy
Multisystem involvement with muscle weakness and developmental delay
references: Rahman S, et al. Combined oxidative phosphorylation defects: clinical and molecular features. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
